title: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
author: Conte ashanti (Ghana)
desc: Anansi l'araignée veut garder toute la sagesse du monde pour lui seul.

p: A long, long time ago, Anansi the spider was clever. But he wanted to be the cleverest in the whole world.
One day, the Sky God, Nyame, gave Anansi a big clay pot. "In this pot, there is all the wisdom of the world," said Nyame. "Share it with everybody."
Anansi looked inside the pot. He saw ideas, stories, answers to every question. He saw how to make fire, how to plant yams, how to cure sickness.
"Share it?" thought Anansi. "No! If I keep it, I will be the only wise one. Everybody will need me!"
Anansi decided to hide the pot at the top of the tallest tree in the forest. Nobody could find it there.
He tied the pot to his belly with a rope, in front of him. Then he started to climb.
But the pot was big and round. It was between Anansi and the tree. He climbed a little and slipped. He climbed again and slipped again.
His little son, Ntikuma, was watching from below. He laughed.
"Father, why don't you tie the pot on your back? Then you can hold the tree with your arms."
Anansi stopped. He was very angry. His little son, a small child, had more wisdom than him — and he had the pot of all the wisdom in the world!
He was so angry that he let go of the pot. It fell from the tree. Crash! It broke into a thousand pieces on the ground.
The wind came. It took the pieces of wisdom and carried them far away. Over the forests, over the rivers, over the villages, all over the world.
And this is why, today, nobody has all the wisdom. Everybody has a little bit. A child, an old woman, a farmer, a king: each one has a small piece.
So when you meet someone, listen to them. Maybe they have the piece of wisdom that you are missing.
